name: Better Planet Generation
summary: A huge planet generation overhaul that aims at making your hundreds of hours of exploration in the magnificent, infinite universe of No Man's Sky less repetitive and hopefully even more memorable.
author: WoodyMontana
description:
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][i][b]                                                     [size=6]Better Planet Generation[/size][/b][/i][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738968-1312445652.jpeg[/img]

[size=4][b]More planets

[/b][size=3]Better Planet Generation is a total overhaul of the planetary generation in No Man's Sky.[/size] [size=3]It improves by a significant margin the procedural aspect of the universe while at the same time respecting the original work and vision from Hello Games.[/size]

[size=3]It adds thousands of new distinct environments to the universe[/size][/size]. All of them come in five different life levels and varying placement scales and layouts. These environments were made to seamlessly combine with each other in many different ways.

Better Planet Generation is designed to bring variety to the different biomes you will visit but most of all it brings a lot of variation to the universe. Outside of the countless combinations of assets and their resulting new environments, planets you visit will present themselves differently each time. Placement layouts, scale of the regions, density, variety of assets and their respective scale, ...

No planet will look exactly the same. Unless, of course, it is a very simple one. More on that below.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1631005159-472402214.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-1789086190.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-1298994048.jpeg[/img]


[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=4][b]Sub Biomes[/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Caves and underwater sub biomes have also been entirely overhauled.

Tons of new variants have been added underground and just like on the surface, additional objects can spawn to increase variety even more.

﻿[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410276-924973523.jpeg[/img]﻿

Underwater has been completely revamped and is now generated through a triple layered dynamic framework combining assets to generate highly varied and detailed environments.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738939-165524032.jpeg[/img]
[b][size=4]
Unique planets

[/size][/b][size=4][size=3]On top of all the added variety, BPG also uses a flexible dynamic generation framework that can take many shapes[/size][/size] and create countless planetary variations, even when the same environments are being used multiple times.

Each planet generated has its own selection of parts based on its biome. Some liberties have been taken when designing and attributing those parts to the various biomes. Some objects have been injected to improve variety, but some restrictions have also been applied to preserve each biome's identity. Better Planet Generation also introduces countless restored, modified or repurposed assets to the game in order to increase the variety while preserving its visual style.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936068-132859967.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-754906087.jpeg[/img]

[/size][/size][/size][/size]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Natural Generation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is a vastly different experience compared to the unmodded game and even other biome mods.
Not even taking into account the small details, it is more than likely that you will never be able to encounter all the possible assets combinations this mod can generate. Let alone in the different regional layouts each dynamic template can result in.

Each biome has access to multiple procedural templates. Each producing different results in terms of layouts and objects combinations.
Their common goal is to show you a different kind of environment each time. Aesthetically and structurally.
No more "postcard" planets where most of what there is to see is right around the corner. The scale of the generation can get extremely vast compared to the vanilla game.

Planetary generation can now affect your visual enjoyment and the gameplay.
It is a video game, after all.

A world generated at its fullest possible level and highest complexity can take you some time to fully explore on foot. Meaning seeing the most notable regions (and not all of them) and scanning everything.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630052272-1155900954.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-2086924238.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630272224-118529207.jpeg[/img]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]More Variation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

On the other hand, Better Planet Generation also allows more simple, generic yet still visually interesting planets to see :

- Planets only covered in grass and some plants, rocks or both.
- More barren worlds dominated by giant stone or crystal spires.
- Radioactive wastelands.
- Planets dotted with trees or occasional small forests.
- Volcanic wastelands.
- Toxic fields.
- Rocky swamps.
- ...

And the list goes on and on.
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3]The occurence of these "generic" planets only relies on probabilites. None of my templates is designed to specifically produce them.
I made sure they still looked good, though.[/size][/size][/size][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410296-1590906166.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1626079315-1486130072.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Different Experience[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is not for everyone. Planets can be both very detailed in every aspect or very simple.
If you expect to always see trees and a full grass coverage on your Lush planet or anywhere else, there are other mods for that.
This is not what you should expect using BPG.

Now, whether you are a new player ready to explore an infinite universe or a more weathered one that wants to be surprised by the game again, I suggest you give Better Planet Generation a try. It won't harm your game in any way.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629923717-282604290.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410307-2137550589.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=5]WARNING BEFORE INSTALLING :[/size][/b]

Installing this mod will operate changes to the terrain in every biomes.
It is also recommended to install it while in a space station / anomaly / freighter and not on a planet's surface.
Some major updates to the mod can reset the terrain or biome lists.
I'll include a warning on the download page and the sticky when it's the case.[/size][/size][/size][/size]


Recommended :
[/size][/size]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/968]DUD's Sky - Colors[/url] : load planetary colour palettes before BPG to avoid procedural textures conflicts.
[/size][/size]

name: AnkhNeter's Clipping Quarters
summary:
SYNTHESIS Compatible v2.22.
Allows wood, concrete, and metal quarter sized floor panels to clip through other objects. No more "INVALID POSITION" when trying to place these objects.
author: Ankh Neter
description:
I created this out of the need to build a proper landing pad using vanilla assets.  There may be others who find it useful in other situations so I'm sharing.
The mod version should match the current public game version.
(See sticky for more information)

[color=#ffff00][size=3]Info:[/size][/color]
This allows the following vanilla building objects to clip through others by disabling the collision check for placement:
-Small Wooden Panel
-Small Concrete Panel
-Small Metal Panel

[color=#ffff00][size=3]History :
[/size][/color]v2.22 - SYNTHESIS Update
v2.16 - Compatiblity version
v2.14 - Compatiblity version
v2.11 - BEYOND Update
v1.77b - Quicksilver Shop Fix
v1.77 - Compatiblity version
v1.76 - Readme added to distribution, no other changes
v1.65 - Compatible version
v1.76 - Initial Release (VISIONS)  

[color=#ffff00][size=3]Credits :[/size][/color]
Of course this wouldn't be possible without the work of [url=https://github.com/monkeyman192/MBINCompiler/releases]monkeyman192[/url] on MBINCompiler
periander for the PSARCTool
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/87374]Lo2k[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/44146502]redmas[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/37637030]RaYRoD118[/url],..I've learned most of my modding by looking into what they are changing in their files.

[color=#ffff00][size=3]Compatibility :[/size][/color]
This mod is incompatible with any mod that modifies \METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\BASEBUILDINGTABLE.MBIN
(Merging may work but not tested)

[color=#ffff00][size=3]Warning:
[/size][/color][color=#f4f4f4]1.[/color][color=#ffff00]  [/color]If the game public version changes/upgrades, please make sure to test that the function of the mod still works before building any new structures.  Easy way to test is to place a wall, then check that the 3 small panels listed above can be placed clipping through the wall.  If so, good to go, if not remove the installed mod and update.  [color=#ffff00][size=3]
[/size][/color]
[color=#ff7700]﻿Reason:[/color] This file holds properties for all of the buildable objects in the game, so new additions have the possibility to put the edits out of order  HG ﻿may changed/added objects properties in this file, which in turn could cause the function to break and cause unintended issues.  Any objects ﻿placed with a mismatched version may possibly need to be deleted and placed with the correct version installed.
[size=3]
2.  [/size]Because collision is disabled on these items, there may be adverse effects if not placed carefully.  e.g. buried in another object. ﻿ ﻿

[color=#ffff00][size=3]Installation:[/size][/color]
1. Download the mod
﻿2. Unzip/open the downloaded file
3. Copy "AnkhNeter's Clipping Quarters v2.22.pak" to your "*\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\MODS\" directory.  (EXML folder is not needed and is only there for reference)
4. Ensure the file "DISABLEMODS.TXT" is either renamed or deleted in "*\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\" directory.
﻿5. ENJOY!

[color=#ffff00][size=3]Removal/Upgrading:[/size][/color]
Because this mod is only changing the collision check on the model for placement, removing this mod or updates should not break any currently built structures.  When the game updates, delete previous version of AnkhNeter's Clipping Quarters and install the matching version.

[color=#ffff00][size=3]My Other Mods:[/size][/color]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/964]AnkhNeter's Clipping Construction[/url] (For those that prefer more modifications.  Do not use both)

name: Fast Actions 7.1
summary: Faster clicks and key pressed actions
author: Lo2k
description:
Instead of pressing a key for almost one second, this mod provides quicker or instant inputs for :
- menu selection
- creating/dismantling technology
- transfering resources to/from ship
- entering ship
- discussing with NPC
- gathering small plants
- launching refinery processing
- recovering deployable technologies

Enjoy !

﻿- instant actions : almost no delay actions (Fractal 4.13 added an in-game option but it only works for a limited range of actions)

name: Exosolar's and Babs' Beyond Base Building
summary: ★ FULLY MP compatible, this mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options
author: Exosolar Sparky NeptuneX3 Babscoole
description:
[b][color=#f1c232][size=4]What is this Mod?[/size][/color][/b]
[size=4]There are now almost 1,000 buildable base parts in vanilla No Man's Sky! It's a dream come true!
This mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options.
This does NOT mean the mod gives you access to all buildable parts.  You still need to learn the blueprints for each.  :)
Beyond Base Building does NOT add any new build parts to the game.

Now includes all the functionality of gBase Items, [color=#ff0000]if chosen by running the Lua script[/color]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Can multiply power, extraction, and storage rates by 2, 5, or 10. WARNING: Bases built with this mod cannot be uploaded for multiplayer when using 2x, 5x, or 10x multiplied rates.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*][size=4]EM Generators do not need a hotspot and produce 250 power.  Not enabled by default.  Must run Lua through ANUMSS and answer question "Choose a multiplier for Storage and Rates and EMAnywhere status" to generate custom mod file to enable.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]

It is [b]fully compatible[/b] with multiplayer, co-op building, uploading, etc, because it [i]does not add[/i] any parts, which would cause issues in multiplayer.[/size]

[size=4][color=#f1c232][b]★ Beyond Basebuilding[/b] is fully Lua scripted, with script provided for easy updating and merging [b]★[/b][/color] and carries over all of the official updates and improvements offered by Hello Games [b]plus[/b]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Most parts can be Scaled [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] prefab building parts, [color=#fff2cc]Exocraft Geobays, Mineral/Gas Extractors and Base Computer[/color] (Door attachment points bug out when scaled, and issues persist with scaled base computers and geobays).  There may be others not listed.  Be aware, scaling breaks snapping.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built in a Freighter.  [color=#fff2cc][i]Exceptions[/i][/color]  include the Base Computer, Industrial Mining parts, Vehicle Summoners and planet-based teleporter.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built at a Planetary Base [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] the freighter teleporter and the Orbital Exocraft Materialiser[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can be built above and below water[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can change color and material[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts, which can be deleted, can be deleted without also deleting attached objects [color=#fff2cc][i]except[/i][/color] Decals and Posters[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]No build-count limits [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] for parts related to resources harvesting, certain terminals, beacons and message capsules (and others with limits that are hard coded into the game, as they are added or changed by Hello Games).[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Unlimited Storage Containers[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*This does not increase actual storage amounts: Each numbered container acts as an index to the store rather than a physical box[/i][/size][/color][/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Foundation, Pavings and Communications Station can be placed anywhere (not only on bare terrain)[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Non corvette parts buildable with corvettes[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]
Some customization of the mod is available just by running it through AMUMSS, where you'll be prompted about enabling several feature.  Even more customization can be had by editing the top portion of the Lua before processing.  See Lua usage below for link to AMUMSS install and basic usage How to.[/size]

[color=#f1c232][b][u][size=5]Disclaimer:[/size][/u][/b][/color]
[size=3]This MOD makes changes to the placement and usage setting of vanilla parts.  If the MOD is removed, the vanilla settings will be restored and parts that "violate" a vanilla setting as well as those connected may go "poof".  Best practice is to regularly backup your saves for semi-painless recovery from the unexpected.[/size]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]

[size=5][b][u][color=#f1c232]Installation[/color]
[/u][/b][/size]
[b]Extract archive contents to GAMEDATA\MODS

[color=#f1c232][size=4][u]Lua usage[/u][/size][/color]
[size=4][b]✦[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2626]How to use AMUMSS at No Man's Sky Nexus - Mods and Community (nexusmods.com)[/url]✦[/b][/size][/b]

[size=4][u][b][color=#f1c232]Modified Files[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[color=#d8d8d8][size=3]METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\BASEBUILDINGOBJECTSTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color]

[i][color=#cccccc][size=3]Also check out...[/size][/color][/i]
[size=5]✦[b][color=#ffdd00][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/58018181?tab=user+files]Exosolar's Other Mods[/url][/color][/b]✦[/size]


[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]

[size=5][u][b][color=#f1c232]Is this Mod up-to-date?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4][i][b]Any mod files which are not hidden or demoted to the "Old Files" area can be expected to work.[/b][/i]
All uploaded files (on the Files page) are maintained with their packing date and version of the MBINCompiler used to pack it. Older mod versions, no longer compatible with the current version of No Man's Sky will be demoted to the "Old Files" subsection, but will remain available for download. There are no side-effects to using this mod.[/size]

[size=4][u][b][color=#f1c232]How to update, tweak, combine, or patch the mod with AMUMSS?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4]As this mod is now Lua scripted, you can [color=#fff2cc]easily [b]update[/b], [b]tweak[/b] or [b]merge[/b] the mod yourself[/color] (if a game update breaks this PAK of the mod, or you have other PAK or Lua mods that could conflict with this one). [color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*Click on the spoiler below for more[/i][/size][/color][/size]
[spoiler]
[size=3][u]Notes on AMUMSS:[/u]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] tries to update [url=https://github.com/monkeyman192/MBINCompiler/releases]MBINcompiler[/url] automatically. If it fails to convert EXML/MBIN files, its likely due to a very recent NMS version update and MBINcompiler is awaiting an update too.
If so, I highly recommend you to disable your mods and wait for MBINCompiler to be updated (it's pretty quick in general).[/size]


[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Updating the mod after a game update:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][list]
[*] [size=3]Download [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url], and extract it locally,  avoid placing the AMUMSS folder in a path with special characters or in a system folder like [color=#fff2cc][i]"C:\Program Files (x86)\(...)"[/i][/color].[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Place the mod Lua script (only the .LUA file, not the .PAK file) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]AMUMSS will normally auto-detect the NMS installation folder, but you can also manually edit the path in the [color=#fff2cc][i]NMS_FOLDER.txt[/i][/color] file.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root of the AMUMSS folder and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]A new modded PAK file will be created, using the last update of the MBIN game files duly amended by the script.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]Most of the time simply recompiling the mod using the Lua script will make it compatible again. Use the latest script to ensure you adopt any mod adjustments to accommodate the latest NMS build.[/size][size=3] There are two main causes of mods not correctly updating with this method:
1) MBINCompiler needs an update to be able to decompile the latest version of the game MBIN files.
2) Structural changes have been made to the MBIN files called by this Lua script. Whilst unlikely, this will require some script rewrite and other mods are likely affected.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Tweaking the mod:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]Use the same process as described in [color=#fff2cc][i]Updating the mod[/i][/color].
Just modify the script as you want before recompiling it. Look at the top of my scripts, you can generally edit modifiers there, or even disable/enable some features very easily.[/size]

[size=3][color=#cccccc][i]*[url=https://notepad-plus-plus.org/]Notepad++[/url] or [url=https://code.visualstudio.com/download/]VSCode[/url] are generally recommended to read EXML and Lua files, due to large file support and automatic highlighting. The [url=https://sourceforge.net/projects/npp-compare/]Compare plugin[/url] for Notepad++, and Lua is also a must-have to highlight file differences.[/i][/color][/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Combining mods that provide Lua scripts:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You'll want to do this if multiple mods affect the same MBIN file.[/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Place all the scripts in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Follow the step, selecting that you want to combine all the scripts into one PAK file, and the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]AMUMSS will output a PAK file that will contain the modifications of all the scripts.[/size]
[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]*If the scripts modify the exact same values in the MBIN file, the last loaded script will overwrite the preceding script values.[/i][/size][/color][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Patch in the mod to make it compatible with other PAK files:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You will want to do this if another mods isn't Lua scripted, and affects the same MBIN file as the Lua scripted mod.

It will work when :
Case 1) you patch a Lua scripted mod for only one other PAK.
Case 2) you patch a Lua scripted mod for several other PAKs, but only if the other PAKs don't modify the same MBIN files between them.[/size]

[size=3][b]How to create a patched PAK:[/b][/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Copy the script and the other mod(s) PAK(s) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS, and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]The new PAK file will contain all the Lua script modifications, and a compatibility patch for the other mod(s) PAK(s).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Rename it something like [color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz Scripted Mod Name -Patched For- The Other Mod Name.pak"[/i][/color].[/size]
[size=3][color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz"[/i][/color] prefix is to ensure that it'll be loaded after the mod(s) it was patched for (for NMS loading order, underscore [i]"_"[/i] came after every other characters).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Remove the original scripted mod PAK from the [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder, and copy both the new patched one, and the other mod(s) PAK(s), into it.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=3][u]Notes:[/u]
[b]Be sure the mod PAK you want to create a compatibility patch for, is updated for the latest NMS version.[/b]
-> When AMUSS find an MBIN file affected by a script and by a PAK in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder, it will take the MBIN file from the mod PAK over the original one of the game, and will apply to it the modifications listed in the script.
So, if the MBIN file of the mod PAK is not updated, the one in the resulting patched PAK won't be either.[/size][/spoiler]
[/spoiler]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]
[color=#f1c232][u][b][size=5]Philosophy[/size][/b][/u][/color]
[size=4]All the erroneous limitations in building are pretty silly, aren't they? In making this mod, I paid specific attention to making sure I did not make changes that will invalidate the bases built with it from online play. Any base made with Beyond BaseBuilding will be fully viable and visible in online play, even when other players don't have this mod! It does this by only editing placement rules while you are in the building editor and not modifying any of the actual base parts themselves.
We hope you enjoy the mod and naturally, your comments are most welcome. We can also be found on the No Man's Sky Discord or reached directly at: [color=#f1c232]Babscoole #6326 [/color]or [color=#f1c232]Exosolar#5120[/color], or if its about the Lua script: [color=#f1c232]NeptuneX3#8095[/color] [size=3][i][size=4]or [/size][/i][/size][color=#f1c232]s p a r k y#0536[/color][/size]

And, of course, thanks to all of the other modders who make mods too, as we often inspect the work of other modders to learn how things are done: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/12249518]RangerDulann[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/1964784]WoodyMontana[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/42286415]jasondude[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/38106355?tab=user+files]Gumsk[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/45932167?tab=user+files]Mjjstral[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/41291360]moddinaccount[/url], Devilin Pixy, saa044, and others have all helped us learn to mod effectively! name: Silent Mod Enabler (formerly VR mod enabler) (Legacy)
summary: Silent mod enabler that disables the mod warning screen while having mods activated.
author: Mjjstral aka MetaIdea - maintenance by Babscoole
description:
Silent mod enabler that disables the mod warning screen while having mods activated.

NMS VR mod enabler\silent mod enabler by Mjjstral (contact: @Mjjstral#1157 on discord)
This tool injects your mods (PCBANKS\MODS folder!) into a original pak and takes care of exact file size to avoid the mod and file tamper warning screens.
Maximum size of all your mod paks should not exceed 5 MB !
Remember to insert the correct path to NMS_PCBANKS_FOLDER.txt !

HOW TO:
1. Download  and extract the tool. Put the tool to the root of the drive where your No Man's Sky is installed to avoid issues. (And don't put the tool files into the PCBANKS folder !)
2. Open NMS_PCBANKS_FOLDER.txt with a text editor and insert your NMS PCBANKS folder path. (....\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS)
3. Make sure all your mods you want to activate are in "No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\MODS"
4. Make sure all mod files together don't exceed 5 MB.
5. Run ENABLE-MODS.bat

Add new mods or when an NMS update hits:
1. Run ENABLE-MODS.bat again.

Change everything back to original files:
1. Run DISABLE-MODS.bat

name: Photon Cannon Sound Mod - Old Robocraft SMGs
summary:
This replaces the photon cannon firing sound with the old fashioned Robocraft laser sounds, and updates English localization to change all instances of "Photon Cannon" to "Subatomic Machine Gun".

I think it fits the gun's style, and I think you'll enjoy it too.
author: Xan the Dragon
description:
[size=6]Photon Cannon => Old Robocraft SMG Sounds[/size]
This mod replaces the photon cannon sounds with the old Robocraft SMG sounds and updates English localization to change all instances of "Photon Cannon" to "Subatomic Machine Gun". Check out the Videos tab for a preview.

[size=3]This mod edits:
[/size]//AUDIO/WINDOWS/NMS_AUDIO_PERSISTENT.BNK (Conflicts can be resolved between mods that edit this! See bottom)
//LANGUAGE/NMS_LOC1_ENGLISH.MBIN



[size=4]Want to make your own sound mods?[/size]
I develop two tools that make this easy! Both of them can be found on [url=https://github.com/XanTheDragon/BNKReplacer]my BNKReplacer GitHub page.[/url]﻿

The first tool is BNKRepacker -- It takes in audio files (Yes, not just WEM files - You don't need to download WWise!*) and packs them into the vanilla BNK file. This does not make new BNK archives as most of the format is undocumented, and existing documentation is horribly out of date.

The second tool is BNKMerger -- It takes in multiple BNK files and allows you to merge them together, sorting out any conflicts in the process. This means you can have multiple audio mods that both modify the same BNK file! See the "Audio Mod Compatibility Guide" text document within this mod's ZIP for more details.

[size=1]* You only need to download WWise if you are replacing the stray WEM files since they use a different format that I do not support yet. If the WEM file goes inside of a BNK, you do not need to download it, but you still can if you want to.[/size]

name: Better Rewards
summary: Increase the amount of currency you get with faster word learning and increased resource gathering options. Frigate (Freighter) Expeditions are also included!
author: MrTrack
description:
Better Rewards increases the amount of units, nanite clusters and quicksilver you get from completing missions or interacting with objects in the world. Non npc word learning (such as knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also faster.

[color=#bf9000][size=3]IMPORTANT NOTE: Don't use this mod when I haven't updated it to the new game version (especially when it is a new or returning expedition)
[/size][/color][color=#bf9000]if you really want to use it when I haven't updated it yet, make sure you [/color][color=#bf9000]back up your save[/color][color=#bf9000] or build the mod using the lua scripts yourself.[/color]

[b]Currency[/b]

Currency gain is roughly increased by 5 times, so as to make it a viable option besides crafting and selling valuable trading goods. Some unit values were tremendously increased (eg.: from minimum amount of 1000-2000 to 20000-50000) like the terminals in abandoned settlements to make the early game less grindy.

Includes:
[list]
[*]Space station missions and Nexus missions
[*]Interactable objects/devices (abandoned buildings, damaged machinery, waypoints, etc.)
[*]Sentinels
[*]Alien interactions
[/list]
[b]Words[/b]

Learning words from non npc interactions (knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also 3 times faster (3 words learned form a single knowledge stone). You now also learn 5 Atlas words, instead of 1 and also have a chance (15%) to learn them when interacting with non npc learning sources.

[b]Resources

[/b]When gathering with the mining beam you generally get 2 times more resources (but only when the things explode as you mine them). Also includes containers, depots, guild rewards, asteroids and ships that drop resources.

[b]Frigate (Freighter) Expedition Rewards

[/b]After a successful expedition, when collecting your rewards you get 5x more units and nanites, 2x more products like Storage Augmentation and NipNip Buds and 3x more resources like Copper, Emeril and Cadmium.
[b]
Installation

[/b]Make sure you delete or edit DISABLEMODS.TXT in your game library (...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS) before trying to use mods. Extract the zip file to ...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder and you are good to go (Create MODS folder if you don't have one). Alternatively you can just use Vortex to download and install.

This mod modifies the [color=#ff0000][size=3]REWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] and [color=#ff0000][size=3]EXPEDITIONREWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] file and will not work with other mods that use those tables.

[b]Updated to NMS version 6.21 (Build ID: 21918502) on 2026.02.13.[/b]

name: GlobalAdjustments
summary: This mode makes combat more challenging by increasing the damage & health of the enemies, adds a harder death penalty aswell as some other small adjustments.
author: Wombi
description:
[b]This mod was lastly created for the LIVING SHIP Update.
If you want a similar mod, check out my new Global Adjustments 2.6 for Desolation update: https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1640/[/b]

This mode makes combat more challenging by increasing the damage & health of the enemies, adds a harder death penalty aswell as some other small adjustments.
[b]
This mod changes the following files:[/b]

METADATA\SIMULATION\SPACE\AISPACESHIPATTACKDATATABLE.MBIN
GCAISPACESHIPGLOBALS.GLOBAL.MBIN
GCCREATUREGLOBALS.MBIN
GCGAMEPLAYGLOBALS.GLOBAL.MBIN
GCPLAYERGLOBALS.GLOBAL.MBIN
GCROBOTGLOBALS.MBIN

[b]Changes:[/b]
- Fights against Pirates are much more difficult.
- Fights against Sentinels (Space) are much more difficult.
- Fights against Sentinels (Planet) are more difficult.
- Fights against Animals are slightly more difficult.
- Player looses 50.000.000 Credits upon death.
- Health recharge starts now a bit later.

name: NomNom
summary: NomNom is the most complete savegame editor for NMS but also shows you additional information around the data you're about to change. You can also easily look up each item individually to examine its attributes, independently of a savegame, or get other useful information that are not related to a specific one (but enhanced if one is loaded).
author: zencq
description:
[color=#e69138][size=3][b]NomNom is now in beta state.[/b] This means for you that some things may still not be 100% finished but the general state of the tool is a lot better than before.[/size] If you encounter bugs or when you think something doesn't work as expected or could be improved, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1566?tab=bugs]let me know[/url]![/color]

[color=#ff0000]All available features are tested while implemented but mistakes can happen, so be aware of that and backup your saves![/color]

The features can be divided into the different main parts:
[list]
[*][b]Manager[/b] Manage your saves!
[list]
[*]Automatic backup.[/*]
[*]Save your save as human-readable JSON.[/*]
[*]Copy, move, and swap slots to another.[/*]
[*]Delete your save.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[*][b]Editor[/b] Edit your save for your needs!
[list]
[*]Ability to manage fleets, change data values like currencies and stats, and organize inventories.[/*]
[*]Ability to fast travel to any system you like, trigger space battles, and clear portal interference.[/*]
[*]Ability to edit your knowledge and recorded experiences.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list]
Have a look at the screenshots as well, to see what NomNom is capable of.

Each version of NomNom is built with the latest game version (at that time) in mind and the version number is reflecting that. Each one is also backwards
compatible down to [b]Beyond 2.11[/b] and even saves before that can still be edited via the build-in JSON editor. If you use it with a newer game version branch than
the one it was built for (e.g. [b]7.00[/b]), things should work as usual in most cases but there can always be a breaking change.

NomNom is compatible with every platform No Man's Sky is available on (some work better than others though). You can select a specific account/folder with you saves or, for platforms on PC, one level above if you have multiple accounts. A complete and always up-to-date overview with additional notes can be found [url=https://github.com/zencq/libNOM.io?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started]on GitHub[/url].


[b]Instructions[/b]
[list=1]
[*]After downloading and extracting the zip file you'll find a few files. All you need to care about is the executable ([b]NomNom.exe[/b]) but new folders may    be created at runtime (e.g. for backups) that will become relevant to you.[/*]
[*]You may want to create a shortcut to the executable for easier access.[/*]
[*]As the tool includes an automatic backup functionality you don't need to do it manually but if you want to be absolutely safe, do it.[/*]
[*]At first start the tool locates your saves at the default location of each platform but if that fails, you must select it manually.[/*]
[*]Select a slot.[/*]
[*]Start tinkering![/*]
[/list]

If you like NomNom and want to support me in its further development, you can do so via the donation options above or on [url=https://www.buymeacoffee.com/cengelha]Buy Me a Coffee[/url], [url=https://github.com/sponsors/cengelha]GitHub[/url], [url=https://ko-fi.com/cengelha]Ko-fi[/url], and [url=https://www.patreon.com/cengelha]Patreon[/url]. I will appreciate it!
There won't be a paywall though.

The is also a dedicated [url=https://discord.gg/nomnom-762409407488720918]Discord[/url] server where you'll find all information in one place, firsthand. Please read the rules first, to gain full access. If you need (or want to offer) help, found a bug, have a suggestion, or something else regarding NomNom, you will find, or can post it there.

Issues created here on Nexus Mods or via another channel will of course also be addressed.


Header image by [url=https://patreon.com/Orioto]Orioto[/url]﻿.

name: Fleet Time Reduce
summary: This mod decreases fleet expeditions time to more sane values.
author: TheLich
description:
[size=3]This mod decreases fleet expeditions time to more sane values.

This mod is scripted version of [url=www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1502]Fleet Expedition Time Reduction[/url] by Ahawk([url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/8972203]xy766[/url]).

Installation:

Copy .pak file from downloaded archive to %GAMEDIR%\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\Mods directory.
If there is no Mods directory - create it.
If there is DISABLEMODS.txt file in %GAMEDIR%\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS directory - remove it or rename it to simething else (ENABLEMODS.txt, for example).

Uninstallation:
Remove FleetTimeReduce.pak from %GAMEDIR%\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\Mods directory.

Files changed:
[b][color=#00ff00]GCFLEETGLOBALS.GLOBAL.MBIN,[/color][/b]
so any mod changing this file will be incompatible - i.e. any mod which tweaks fleet values.

Mod assembled with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url], lua file included.[/size]

name: Burryaga's Blooming Biomes
summary: This mod dramatically increases the presence of flora and fauna throughout No Man's Sky. No terrain is modded, making this vanilla-friendly for use in multiplayer. Blooming Biomes is compatible with Frontiers, as well as a wide variety of quality-of-life and graphical-enhancement mods.
author: Burryaga
description:
[center][center][b][size=5]Burryaga's Blooming Biomes[/size]
[/b][size=3][i]Ready for Frontiers (v3.68)![i][size=3]

[/size][/i](NO LONGER BEING UPDATED; YOU WILL NEED TO FOLLOW MANUAL UPDATE INSTRUCTIONS IN THE FAQ; SORRY)[/i][/size]

[size=2]This mod will cause many more plants and animals to spawn on most planet types, especially lush worlds. It accomplishes this by modifying fields for [/size][b]Coverage[/b][size=2], [/size][b]CoverageType[/b][size=2], [/size][b]FlatDensity[/b][size=2], and [/size][b]SlopeDensity [/b][size=2]in the lists of [/size][b]GcEnvironmentSpawnData [/b][size=2]found in [/size][b]METADATA/SIMULATION/SOLARSYSTEM/BIOMES/[/b][size=2] (the location of data about biome-specific object types), as well as modifying fields for [/size][b]MinGroupSize[/b][size=2], [/size][b]MaxGroupSize[/b][size=2], and [/size][b]Density [/b][size=2]in the [/size][b]GcCreatureRoleDescriptionTable [/b][size=2]objects found in [/size][b]METADATA/SIMULATION/ECOSYSTEM/[/b][size=2] (the location of data about biome-specific animal types). Any other mod that affects the files in these folders may conflict with this mod.[/size]

[size=2]The screenshots explain the mod better than any words I know.

[/size][i]Like this mod? Try my mod pack, [/i][i][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2069]Burryaga's Best Buds[/url][b]﻿[/b][/i][i], and have way more fun exploring these blooming biomes![/i]

[size=2]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[/size][size=2][b][i]Latest News:[/i][/b][i] Frontiers v3.68 is out, and it fixes many basic bugs from the initial Frontiers release. Grab it today![/i]

[i]New versions of Alien Colours are available that reuse the game's Crystal palettes as Space palettes. Space will be more colorful, so if black space is your thing, you'll probably want to stick to the original versions of these mods (which I repacked for 3.68).
[/i]
[i]If you ensure that Blooming Biomes loads *after* other mods﻿, this should merge very well and also render other mods multiplayer-friendly. An easy way to force load order is to prefix the names of any mods you want loading first with a hyphen (-). You can also prefix any mods you want to load last with a tilde (~). For best results, I recommend you load [/i][b][i]Blooming Biomes[/i][/b][i] and [/i][b][i]Bloom Protector[/i][/b][i] last. [/i][b][i]Bloom Protector[/i] [/b][i]will only work if it is loaded [/i][b]after [/b][i]other files that modify either [/i][b][i]VOXELGENERATORSETTINGS.MBIN[/i][/b][i] or [/i][b][i]BIOMES/PLACEMENTVALUES/SPAWNDENSITYLIST.MBIN[/i][/b][i] in [/i][b][i]METADATA/SIMULATION/SOLARSYSTEM/[/i][/b][i]. I intend to add protection against other changes in the future.[/i]

[b][i]Note:[/i][/b] [i]I have experienced enormous frame drops (from [b]105 fps[/b] to [b]40 fps[/b]) using recent releases of[/i] [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2053][i]Sci Fi Fantasy Core[/i][/url]﻿[i], so, even though I know the combination looks quite lovely in places, please consider trying [/i][b][i]Blooming Biomes[/i][/b][i] by itself if you experience frame issues in combination with any other mods. I intend to make contact with the creator of[/i][b] [/b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2053][i]Sci Fi Fantasy Core[/i][/url]﻿[i] in order to determine how this performance issue can be fixed.[/i]

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size]

[size=2]The downloadable .zip (installable via [/size][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/about/vortex/]Vortex[/url]﻿[size=2]) comes with [b][i]two editions[/i][/b] of [b]Blooming Biomes[/b], each of which has [b]four [/b]variations:[/size]

[i][b][size=3]Global Forests Edition[/size]
[/b][i]
[b]BloomingBiomes-[i][i][b]GlobalForests[/b][/i][/i][i][b]-NormalFlora-OriginalSpecies[/b][/i][/b][/i][b][i][b][i][b]
[b]BloomingBiomes-GlobalForest-NormalFlora-NewSpecies[/b][/b][/i][/b][/i][/b]
[b]BloomingBiomes-GlobalForest-BiggerFlora-OriginalSpecies
[b]BloomingBiomes-GlobalForests-BiggerFlora-NewSpecies[/b][/b][/i]

[i][b][size=3]Expanded Forests Edition[/size]
[/b][/i]
[b][i]BloomingBiomes-ExpandedForests-NormalFlora-OriginalSpecies
BloomingBiomes-ExpandedForests-NormalFlora-NewSpecies
BloomingBiomes-ExpandedForests-BiggerFlora-OriginalSpecies
BloomingBiomes-ExpandedForests-BiggerFlora-NewSpecies

[/i][/b]I also include [b]four[/b] variations of [b]Flourishing Fauna[/b] (a mod that can moderately increase both the population and size of all animals), as well as [b]Bloom Protector[/b] (an [b]inhibitor mod[/b] that will enable this mod to look better with other mods).

[i]An [/i][b][i]inhibitor mod[/i][/b][i] is installed normally, and works by simply ensuring that a vanilla file remains vanilla. Mods that modify the same MBIN file as previously loaded mods will "inhibit" the prior mod by replacing their changes to the game. The [b]~[/b] in [b]~BloomProtector[/b] ensures that it loads after most mods. You can also affect load order using normal alphabetization, underscores[i] (for loading mods late)[/i], and hyphens[i] (for loading mods early)[/i].[/i]

[size=2]When you figure out which [b].paks[/b] you want to use and extract it from the .zip, you can rename them freely.[/size]

[i][size=3]I will refer to your final selected version of [b]Blooming Biomes [/b]as [b]BloomingBiomes.pak[/b] in the instructions below.[/size][/i]

[b][i][size=4]~~~ Warning ~~~[/size]

[size=2]If you are concerned about having new flora to scan on all of your old planets, then [u]do not[/u] use the New Species versions of Burryaga's Blooming Biomes![/size][/i][/b]

[size=2][i]These versions of this mod use SwapPrimaryForRandomColour in GcObjectSpawnData. This will actually cause [/i][u]entirely new species of plants[/u][i] to appear on your planets [/i][u]while the mod is running[/u][i], and any plants found during this time will be [/i][u]permanently[/u][i] added to your Discoveries. You will see them in Discoveries with or without the mod, but you will only be able to scan them while the mod is running. Similarly, you will only be able to scan vanilla flora while the mod is [b]not [/b]running.[/i][/size]

[b]You have been warned. :D[/b]

[size=2]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size]

[size=4][b]Blooming Biomes Editions and Variations[/b][size=2][size=4]

[/size][size=2][b][i]Global Forests Edition[/i] — [/b]The craziest floral bloom. This is the full experience: worldwide forests of trees and shrooms, with a range of increased coverages of various other flora. Grass planets will become jungles. Prepare to need to clear land for building in some areas. Formerly called the [i]Full Bloom Edition[/i].[/size][size=4]

[/size][b][i]Expanded Forests Edition[/i][/b][b] — [/b]Some people feel the full bloom is too many trees and shrooms, and some people simply struggle to run the full bloom with their usual graphics settings. The [i]Expanded Forests Edition[/i] allows those people to experience something between vanilla No Man's Sky and the [i]Global Forests Edition[/i] of Blooming Biomes. Formerly called the [i]Weeping Lorax Edition.[/i][size=4][size=2]

[/size][/size][b][i]New Species Variation[/i] — [/b]This variation will change your flora to new species of flora, as stated above in the warning.[size=4][size=2]

[/size][/size][b][i]Bigger Flora Variation[/i] — [/b]This variation will make virtually all flora significantly bigger (the size changes are not applied to animals, although I have considered doing this as well in the future). Mushrooms are massively bigger, trees about double in size. Other flora such as bush, flowers, and grass are resized a bit more modestly.

[size=2]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size]

[size=4][b]Optional Enhancements[/b][/size]

[b][i]Flourishing Fauna [/i]— [/b]All versions increase the group sizes of animals, raise maximum spawnable number of fauna, and decrease the delay between spawns. Variations of this mod can also increase the size of fauna significantly (but not massively).

[b][i]Alien Colours [/i]— [/b]All eight variations of [b]Alien Colours[/b] will drastically alter the palettes of the game, resulting in a more colorful and surreal experience. I chose these colors by testing how they look together in game for many hours, so I think people who relate to my preferences will really love what I've done. The palettes are simply rearranged in each version to give you a better chance of getting a color you especially love at your favorite base. [b]Alpha[/b], [b]Beta[/b], [b]Gamma[/b], and [b]Delta[/b] now have four updated versions that affect the Colours of the Space palettes. The new versions are named [b]Epsilon[/b], [b]Zeta[/b],[b] Eta[/b], and [b]Theta[/b], respectively.

[b][i]Chaos Colours [/i]— [/b]Want an even crazier experience? Try [b]Chaos Colours[/b], which totally randomizes almost all of the palettes in the game (meaning every palette that can safely be randomized without causing connection issues in multiplayer). [b][i]Even your ships will be new colors while this mod is running.[/i][/b] This comes in dark, medium, and unlimited color variations (the last of which is capable of generating jet black, blinding white, and every other RGB color between them). Try rebuilding [b]Chaos Colours [/b]in [url=https://github.com/cmkushnir/NMSModBuilder]Mod Builder[/url]﻿ and changing the seed to get a completely unique and totally unpredictable color experience that no one else has ever had before (unless you use popular numbers I may have already tried)![/size][/size]

[size=2]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size]

[size=4][b]Installation Process[/b]

[/size][size=2]The first few steps are the same for everyone: download the .zip from [/size][b]FILES[/b][size=2], and unzip it somewhere.[/size]

[size=2]You will now have access to four .pak files. Decide which version of the mod to try, and rename it [/size][b]BloomingBiomes.pak[/b][size=2].[/size][b]

[/b][size=2]The process for installing this .pak varies slightly, depending on whether you are using the Steam or Windows Store version of No Man's Sky. Follow the instructions below that are relevant to you.[/size]

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[b][i][size=3]Installation Process for Steam Users[/size][/i]
[/b]
[size=2]Navigate to [/size][b]Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS[/b][size=2].[/size]

[size=2]I cannot tell you where you installed Steam, but mine is in [/size][b]C:\Program Files (x86)[/b][size=2].[/size]

[size=2]In [/size][b]PCBANKS[/b][size=2], rename [/size][b]DISABLEMODS.TXT [/b][size=2]to [/size][b].DISABLEMODS.TXT[/b][size=2] (notice the leading period), [/size][b]or just delete this file entirely[/b][size=2]. The game will not care [/size][i]at all[/i][size=2] if this file ceases to exist (it's callous like that). You can disable individual mods, such as the one you're about to install, by simply moving or hiding them.[/size]

[b]Move[/b][size=2] or [/size][b]copy[/b][size=2] your desired version of [/size][b]BloomingBiomes.pak[/b][size=2] into [/size][b]PCBANKS\MODS\[/b][size=2].[/size]

[size=2]That's it! Installing mods is easy on Steam.[/size]

[size=2]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size]

[b][i][size=3][b][i]Installation Process for [/i][/b]Windows Store Users[/size][/i]

[/b][size=2]Ultimately, the idea is simple (and almost identical to the Steam method):[/size]

[b]Navigate [/b][size=2]to [/size][b]GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\ [/b][size=2]in your game installation directory.[/size]

[size=2]In [/size][b]PCBANKS[/b][size=2], rename [/size][b]DISABLEMODS.TXT [/b][size=2]to [/size][b].DISABLEMODS.TXT[/b][size=2] (notice the leading period), [/size][b]or just delete this file entirely[/b][size=2]. The game will not care [/size][i]at all[/i][size=2] if this file ceases to exist (it's callous like that). You can disable individual mods, such as the one you're about to install, by simply moving or hiding them.[/size]

[b]Navigate [/b][size=2]to [/size][b]GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\MODS\ [/b][size=2]in your game installation directory.[/size]

[b]Move [/b][size=2]or [/size][b]copy [/b][size=2]your desired version of [/size][b]BloomingBiomes.pak [/b][size=2]into this folder.[/size]

[size=2]Then you're golden![/size]

[i]However[/i][size=2], the location of [/size][i]your game installation directory[/i][size=2] is a bit odd and possibly unique when you use the Microsoft Store. The folder's naming conventions are unclear to me. I use Steam, so my knowledge of this process is entirely secondhand.[/size]

[size=2]I have been told that [/size][b]GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\MODS\[/b][size=2] is located in the following convoluted location:[/size]

[size=2][b]﻿%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\HelloGames.NoMansSky_ODD-SUFFIX\LocalCache\Local\Microsoft\WritablePackageRoot\[/b][/size]

[b][b][size=2]ODD-[/size][/b][/b][size=2][b]SUFFIX [/b]is a string of seemingly random numbers and letters, and may not be the same for all users. Therefore, you need to first explore [b]%localappdata%\Packages\[/b] in order to determine the precise name of your [b]HelloGames.NoMansSky[/b] folder, and then add the rest of that folder address. Furthermore, in order to affect the game by accessing this folder in the first place, you may need this program:[/size]

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1751]ANMSMEMSPC - Andy's NMS Mod Enabler for the Microsoft Store Edition (Xbox GamePass PC)[/url]

[size=2]The above program may deal with [/size][b]DISABLEMODS.TXT [/b][size=2]for you.[/size]

[size=2]Sorry, Microsoft Store people. I have heard that things are not so easy for you guys, but they are doable with persistence.[/size]

[size=2]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size]

[b][size=3]Installation Process for Vortex Users[/size][/b]

[i](Even though you probably already know.)[/i]

[b]Launch[/b][size=2] the app and log into [/size][b]Vortex[/b][size=2].[/size]

[size=2]Add [/size][i][b]No Man's Sky[/b][/i][size=2] to [b]GAMES [/b]if you have not already done so.

[/size][b]Navigate[/b] to [b]MODS[/b].

[b]Drag & Drop[/b][b] [/b]the Blooming Biomes .zip file into the dotted box where you see, "Drop File(s)" (bottom of the app).

[b]Click[/b][i] [/i]the button labeled Never Installed[i] [/i](not the arrow, the actual words).

[b]Choose [/b]which version of the mod you would prefer to try, and then [b]Finish[/b].

Click the button labeled Disabled. It will become [b]Enabled[/b].

That's it!

[size=2]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size]

[b][size=4]Frequently Asked Questions[/size][/b]

[b][size=3][i]Will this affect my framerate?[/i] [/size][/b]

[size=2]This is an extremely new mod, and I have obviously not had time to thoroughly test it on Frontiers. Please contact me if you have any major issues on modern graphics cards. If you're trying to run Ultra everything on a card older than a GTX 1080, good luck with that; obviously, generating more of everything is not computationally "free", and you should not expect an identical framerate to vanilla No Man's Sky. However, I have done my best to make sure that everywhere I visit is stable and smooth on my MSI 2080 Super Trio, so you will probably have great results on anything as good or better than that. I have also enlisted the help of testers who can confirm that this mod works on anything as good as a GTX 1080, but you may need to adjust settings.[/size]

[b][size=3][i]Will this make me crash more?[/i][/size][/b][i][b][i]

[/i][/b][/i][size=2]It should never make you crash. If you [/size][b][i]do[/i][/b][size=2] crash anywhere unusual, please contact me! I will determine why so that I can patch the issue as soon as possible. Please note that some people have discovered unusual crashing in vanilla Frontiers, so it will be helpful if you can confirm with certainty that the mod is your reason for any crashes before you contact me.[/size]

[b][size=3][i]Are these changes permanent?[/i][/size]

[/b][size=2]Yes and no. The changes to game files (the biome updates and animal group size increases) are [/size][i]not[/i][size=2] permanent. These will go away when you disable the mod. However, as mentioned above, updates to your Discoveries [/size][i]are permanent[/i][size=2] after you save your game.
[/size]
[size=3][b][i]Are there any known issues with the mod?[/i][/b]
[/size]
[size=2]Nothing game-breaking. However, collision detection on spawned objects can be inconsistent. Most objects will spawn with collision, but I have found patches of objects that seem to be missing collision detection. Also, some large objects have poor collision detection on their top surface (even in vanilla, for the record), so standing on them for screenshots is a bit of a fine art. Also, you will see some tree-type plants growing into or through each other. This is inevitable, and, for me, a small price to pay for what the mod brings.

[/size][b][i][size=3]I'm seeing rectangular patches of grassless terrain. Did you do that?[/size]

[/i][/b][size=2]No, Frontiers did that. They can also be found in vanilla.

[b][i][size=3]The elevation of my settlement just changed slightly. Did you do that?[/size][/i][/b]

[size=2]No, Frontiers did that. This change arrived with the introduction of the new Expedition in 3.63.[/size][/size]

[b][i][size=3]A phantom tree is growing in my base and I can't hit it with the mining beam. Can I do anything about this?[/size]

[/i][/b][size=2]Use the terrain manipulator to destroy the phantom tree's foundation, then repair the ground. Not a perfect solution, but, again, that's a price that I am happily willing to pay in order to run this mod.[/size]

[b][i][size=3]Are any updates planned?[/size]

[/i][/b][size=2]Probably. MBIN Compiler has officially been repaired to the point that Blooming Biomes is in complete working order for Frontiers (thanks to the amazingly dedicated efforts of the MBC team for their incredible efficiency). However, I do want to continue exploring objects that will look good when I increase their coverage without doing too much harm to frame rates, especially on non-lush worlds.[/size]

[b][i][size=3]Will the updates break my bases?
[/size]
[/i][/b][size=2]Break, no. [i]However[/i], you may have some new trees or shrooms growing [i]through[/i] your base. I will never do any terrain edits. Future updates will be aimed at balancing density to reduce the frequency of stuff growing through each other and increase proportion of objects that properly spawn with vanilla collision (meaning never expect perfection here), rebalancing plants a bit so that the rarer pretty stuff grows more frequently, and, of course, attempting to save as many frames per second as possible in order to enable as many people as possible to enjoy this mod together! I appreciate any suggestions regarding performance enhancements.

[/size][i][size=3]Is there anything I can do to improve performance?[/size]

[/i][size=2]Maybe. You can try to follow these steps, and hope for the best. [i]It will not work for everyone[/i]. For me, I gained about 10 FPS on average, give or take 5, depending on the scenario. This honestly blew my mind. This fix involves modifying a game settings file in a text editor in order to allow No Man's Sky to use more of your GPU threads (assuming I understand the field's name correctly). If you do not have more threads than No Man's Sky is already using, this might not help you. I am not completely sure, but I suspect No Man's Sky may use less than the actual maximum number of threads by default for some GPUs. This setting, apparently in beta judging by its name, seems to allow use of all or at least more of your threads.

[b]Navigate[/b] to your game installation directory, where you will find two folders: [b]Binaries[/b] and [b]GAMEDATA[/b].

Navigate to [b]Binaries/SETTINGS[/b].

[b]Open[/b] the file named [b]TKGRAPHICSSETTINGS.MXML[/b] in any text editor. I use Atom and Code.

Find the following line in [b]TKGRAPHICSSETTINGS.MXML[/b]:

[b]<Property name="NumGraphicsThreadsBeta" value="0" />[/b]

Set the [b]value[/b] of the above [b]Property [/b]to the [b]value[/b] of either the [b]Property [/b]element named [b]NumHighThreads[/b] or the one named [b]NumLowThreads[/b] (these had the same values for me, but pick the higher value if there is one), and launch the game.

As implied by its [b]Beta [/b]status, I can tell you that [i][b]this adjustment will not work for everyone[/b][/i]. [i]You may crash[/i]. However, when I set the [b]value[/b] of this [b]Property [/b]to [b]12[/b], I saw a clear performance boost of about 10 fps on average.

Note that [b]Property [/b]elements [b]NumHighThreads[/b] and [b]NumLowThreads[/b] will revert to their default values upon launching the game, so they can't help you any further; [b]NumGraphicsThreadsBeta[/b] is all we have. Spare yourself the trouble of trying them.

Why 12? Why [b]NumHighThreads[/b]? Well, I tested quite a bit and found similar performance improvements at both the 12 and 16 level. Since the number of threads intuitively appears to refer to a CPU variable, Chris Kushnir (author of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2032]NMS Mod Builder[/url]) hypothesized that it may be referring to the number of CPU threads that can push requests to the [i]GPU[/i] (hence [b]NumGraphicsThreads[/b]). Based on my own testing, I hypothesize that this value is capped by either [b]NumHighThreads [/b]or [b]NumLowThreads[/b], and, unfortunately, as stated before, changes to those fields appear to revert.

If this helps, let other people know! If it doesn't, sorry! I wish I could help, but I have no way of forcing it to work when it fails.

[b][size=3][i]Which version of this mod do you use?[/i][/size][/b]

[size=2]My favorite is the one with larger stuff and randomized colors, but I don't really care about my Discoveries featuring nonexistent entities. (See warning above if you have no idea what I mean.) For me, it's super fun to see a bunch of new stuff on all of my old planets, so I don't care if a few species are missing while I run the recolored versions.[/size]

[b][size=3][i]Which versions of Mod Builder and MBIN Compiler did you use?[/i][/size][/b]
[/size][size=2]
I used [url=https://github.com/cmkushnir/NMSModBuilder/releases/download/v.2.1.2/NMSModBuilder.7z]Mod Builder v2.1.2[/url] with [url=https://github.com/monkeyman192/MBINCompiler/releases/download/v3.68.0-pre2/libMBIN.dll]MBIN Compiler v3.68.0-pre2[/url]﻿﻿ ([b]libMBIN:3.68.0.2[/b], [b]NMS:2021-09-28[/b]).﻿

Also, you must add [i]the following line[/i] to [b]cmkNMSReleases.txt[/b] and replace [b]libMBIN.dll[/b] in [b]NMSModBuilder [/b]with [b]v3.68.0.2 [/b]from the [b]MBIN Compiler[/b] link above:

[i]3.68, Frontiers, 2021-09-28, 3.68.0.2, v3.68.0-pre2[/i][i][/i]

[b][size=4]Special Thanks

[/size][/b][/size][size=2]I want to thank a number of other modders who have made this mod possible for me. [/size]

[size=2]First and foremost, this mod was made using Chris Kushnir's [/size][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2032]NMS Mod Builder[/url][size=2]. That program is amazing and extremely helpful for anyone with C# experience. His libraries for packing my C# code into meaningful game data were fundamental to me being able to do this at all. And his app's ability to safely handle incomplete game data allowed me to have this mod ready for playing around in Frontiers before any updates to MBIN Compiler were live.[/size][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2032]

[/url][size=2]I also want to thank the modding community of the [/size][url=https://discord.gg/22ZAU9H]No Man's Sky Modding Discord[/url][size=2]﻿ as well as the [/size][url=https://discord.gg/nomanssky]No Man's Sky Discord[/url][size=2]﻿ (especially its [/size][b]#modding[/b][size=2] channel) for being awesome and helpful and supportive of new modders. Thanks in particular to several modders who have helped me personally understand various technical issues related to modding No Man's Sky, including Mjjstral, Gumsk, monkeyman192, RayRod, WinderTP, and WoodyMontana. I would also like to give a shoutout to Argh, Exosolar, and jasondude7116 (also known as Dud) for creating some amazing mods that make my screenshots so much better.[/size]

[size=2]Thanks as well to all of the programming legends who make MBIN Compiler work (especially monkeyman192 and WBertro, as well as the mysterious emoose, whom I do not know personally but who definitely worked on earlier versions of MBIN Compiler). They comprise a small group of very hardworking programmers who make NMS modding a possibility for most of us. They can't possibly get enough credit for the possibilities they've brought to No Man's Sky.[/size]

[size=2]Finally, thanks to the many people who have been willing to help me test the mod and fix early crashes while I figured out what I could get away with modding, and how much I could get away with modding it. The early versions were less stable than what anyone on Nexus will be trying, and I appreciate their willingness to try and crash and try again. Their reports helped make this mod much more reliable than it would otherwise be. I truly appreciate you all.

[size=2]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/size]

files.name: Blooming Biomes
files.description: Latest version of Blooming Biomes, ready for 3.66! I have fixed a small issue in my shroom propagation that may have reduced your frame rate significantly on heavily shroom-covered planets. I have also included a new inhibitor and separated animal mods.
files.changelog_html:
Updated version numbering system for 3.66. Version numbers will now match the game version for which they were built.
Improved biome generation in shroom worlds to recover a lot of frames. I had accidentally propagated a certain class of shroom far more than intended or desired.

files.name: Blooming Biomes
files.description: Latest version of Blooming Biomes, ready for 3.67! The separate animal mods now come in four flavors, and there is also a pack of new color mods you can try!
files.changelog_html:
Renamed files to be more descriptive and less cheeky. (I know like 3 of us snickered at the Weeping Lorax filename, but for a lot of other people in the world it just seemed to bring confusion.) Full Bloom -> Global Forests. Weeping Lorax -> Expanded Forests. Flora Recolored -> New Species. Nothing Recolored -> Original Species. Resized Flora -> Bigger Flora. More Fauna -> Flourishing Fauna (now also has resizing options). Normal Animals implies normal sizes, Bigger Animals implies the obvious. Normal Flourish and Extra Flourish refer to the increase in population relative to vanilla.
Reuploaded latest version in an attempt to get the version number to appear accurately. No changes from first version of 3.67.

1.0: Initial public version of Blooming Biomes.
Rearranged zip options, renamed available paks to more clearly describe what they do and match Edition - Variation format.
Added an experimental version as a Vortex-ready .zip in preparation for new distribution package. When 3.63 is stable, 1.1 will be a single Vortex-friendly .zip including a source folder.
3.66: Updated version numbering system for 3.66. Version numbers will now match the game version for which they were built.
Improved biome generation in shroom worlds to recover a lot of frames. I had accidentally propagated a certain class of shroom far more than intended or desired.
3.67: Renamed files to be more descriptive and less cheeky. (I know like 3 of us snickered at the Weeping Lorax filename, but for a lot of other people in the world it just seemed to bring confusion.) Full Bloom -> Global Forests. Weeping Lorax -> Expanded Forests. Flora Recolored -> New Species. Nothing Recolored -> Original Species. Resized Flora -> Bigger Flora. More Fauna -> Flourishing Fauna (now also has resizing options). Normal Animals implies normal sizes, Bigger Animals implies the obvious. Normal Flourish and Extra Flourish refer to the increase in population relative to vanilla.
Reuploaded latest version in an attempt to get the version number to appear accurately. No changes from first version of 3.67.
3.68: Fixed error in Flourishing Fauna that caused excessive animal population increase and resulted in greater than expected frame drops.

name: BuildFrame RecTUM - Recategorisation and Trimming Utility for Build Menu
summary: Recategorises and condense vanilla basebuilding menu groups to make room for modded objects. The backbone of BuildFrame.
author: WinderTP and Babscoole
description:
[center][b][font=Lucida Sans Unicode][size=6]RecTUM[/size]
[size=5][u](Recategorisation and Trimming Utility for Build Menu)[/u]

[b]is the backbone of[/b]
[u][img]https://i.imgur.com/gy8ND8k.png[/img][/u][/size][/font][/b][/center][center][b][font=Lucida Sans Unicode][size=5]﻿﻿﻿﻿[size=4][b]A framework focused on integrating various basebuilding mods into one playable and accessible environment.
[/b][/size][/size][/font][/b][size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2197][/url][/size][size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2197]RecTUM - Recategorisation and Trimming Utility for Build Menu[/url]﻿
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2215]SACS - Selection Augmentation for Colour System
[/url][/size][size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2281][s]WENIS - Wall Elements eNforced Intact-keeping or Substitution
[/s][/url][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2604]MILF - Build Menu Infrastructure Listings from Foundation[/url][/size][size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2281][/url][/size][/center]




[u][b][size=6]Why make RecTUM?[/size][/b][/u]

[size=3]Since the 3.7 update, the build menu has been revamped into a "tab and list" structure, there are 11 vanilla "top groups" at the time of writing.

Through some research, we discovered that the maximum number of top groups that can appear in the build menu is [u][b]19[/b][/u]. Once the amount of internal top groups exceeds that number, they are either inaccessible to players in-game, or would cause instabilities, to the point of crashing the game when opening the build menu.

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/ESTohOv.png[/img]﻿[/center]
At the same time, each top group has a display size limit of around [u][b]24 rows of objects[/b][/u], with the limit decreasing with more subgroups taking room by opening with a new row. We've also found the maximum functional limit of objects per top group is [b][u]240[/u][/b].  Once again, exceeding that limit will cause instabilities, including inaccessible objects, the build menu UI bugging out visually, booting players out of selected top groups, or crashes.

With the vanilla groups untouched, the absolute maximum number of modded base objects would be [b][u][b][u]240*8=1920 [/u][/b]objects[/u][/b]. With current basebuilding mods, we are already past 2000 objects, and thus necessitates a change in the vanilla groups to make room for modded objects in order to maintain compatibility, stability of the mods, and various quality-of-life features such as distinct categorisation, proper headers, etc.

[b][u]RecTUM condenses the vanilla categories into 5 top groups.[/u][/b] This means 6 vanilla top groups are hidden from the build menu, and the [b][u]total free space for new top groups is now 14[/u][/b]. This creates a space for mods that add new base objects to expand more freely, without the fear of crashing the game.
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/OY6aLJ9.png[/img][/center][/size]

[b][u][size=6]Installation[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]RecTUM is not meant to be used standalone, even though it can be; it is intended to be used in conjunction with one and more basebuilding mods that add additional objects to the build menu.

[b][u]RecTUM is designed to be used as an AMUMSS .lua script[/u][/b], to be used along with any .luas that other basebuilding mods provide. However, [b][u]an installable version is also available[/u][/b] for those who not versed to using AMUMSS.[/size]


[size=6][center][url=https://stepmodifications.org/wiki/NoMansSky:Tutorials/HowToAMUMSS]How To merge with AMUMSS[/url]
[url=https://stepmodifications.org/wiki/NoMansSky:Tutorials/Merging_two_mods]How to merge without AMUMSS[/url]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2626]How to use AMUMSS (pdf)[/url][/center][/size]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957][size=5][b][center]Click here to go to AMUMSS's Nexus mod page.[/center][/b][/size][/url]

[size=4]When used alone, the output mod name will be [b][u]"~~~BuildFrame_RecTUM"[/u][/b]; if incorrectly combined by AMUMSS in conjunction with other luas, the mod name will be [b][u]"++++DO_NOT_COMBINE_IN_AMUMSS"[/u][/b] (or whatever the last lua that dictates the MOD_BATCHNAME to be)[/size]


[b][u][size=6]Compatibility[/size][/u][/b]
[size=3]
RecTUM is designed to be [b][u]processed early in AMUMSS[/u][/b], before most other scripts. The intention is that the vanilla groups be reduced before any other tweak is done, although it is not essential.

Because it is processed before any other script, RecTUM edits only the vanilla base object entries (specifically, which group they belong to) and adds new "sub-groups" into existing vanilla top groups.

Because the reduced sub-groups are not removed, only hidden, mods adding objects to said vanilla groups will still show the objects under their intended vanilla groups.

[b]Any modders who ultilises AMUMSS lua scripts and want their base objects added to vanilla groups moved by RecTUM should name their lua script with 7 (seven) plus signs (+) at the beginning of the file name. For more information, feel free to join the [url=https://discord.gg/kFxjuuj]modding discord[/url] and discuss with us further.[/b]

name: Old Style Slots 3.3
summary: Restores old style slots
author: Lo2k
description:
Everybody noticed that inventories and inventory slots have changed with Waypoint Update.
If we can't fully restore the old style inventories, we can at least restore a few of the old features and this mod is made for that.

What this mod does :
- replaces the big numbers "Count / Max" or "Charge%" by the old small count number over a little bar or just the recharge bar
- removes the new down right dark corner
- restores flat background colors


What it doesn't do though :
- it doesn't restore the rectangular slots with the name of the item
- it doesn't change the 4.0 inventory layout

At least, the old style was more visual, gave more visibility to the item picture and was less cluttered with numbers.

Optional :
- Improve visibility of empty slots with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2526/][color=#ffd966]Better Empty Slots
[/color][/url]- Improve visibility of supercharged slots with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2556/][color=#ffd966]Better Supercharged Slots
[/color][/url]- Improve visibility of broken and overloaded slots with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2586][color=#ffd966]Better Broken and Overloaded Slots[/color][/url]


[b]This mod has been updated for Worlds Part 2 new modding scheme.[/b]

name: Detailed Base Computer Screen
summary: Changes base screen computer from green lines to readable text.
author: Virtual Voyager
description:
[b]Description:[/b] This mod simply changes the base computer screen from green scrolling lines to actual text. In addition to this, the text now scrolls upwards instead of downwards and moves at a much slower pace. Two versions are currently included, one with a green background (like vanilla) and one with a black background (looks like an old DOS display).

[b]Changelog: 1.1[/b]
[list]
[*]Changed "Initializing" to "Initialising" to fit NMS spelling style.
[*]Corrected spelling of "Compatability" to "Compatibility".
[/list]
[b]Modifies: 

[/b]MODELS\PLANETS\BIOMES\COMMON\BUILDINGS\PARTS\BUILDABLEPARTS\BASECOMPUTER\BASECOMPUTER\[b]LIGHTS_MAT.MATERIAL.MBIN[/b]
TEXTURES\PLANETS\BIOMES\COMMON\BUILDINGS\SHARED\BUILDABLEBUILDINGS\[b]MINISCREEN.BASE.1.DDS[/b] [i](CUSTOM TEXTURE RENAMED TO MINI.VV.DDS)

[/i]Special thanks to [b]SlippyCheeze and WinderTP [/b]in the NMS Modding Discord, who helped me find the texture for the base computer screen!

name: JE's Tiny Volcano
summary: Tired of being sent to a quest objective only to find that it is inside of a volcano?  Me too!   This mod does only one thing.  It shrinks volcanoes to 10% of their original size, so that you can access the quest objective.
author: Jaggid Edje
description:
This mod shrinks volcanoes to 10% of their normal size.   The purpose of it being, so I can get to those pesky quest objective locations that are INSIDE some random volcano.  It looks funky, and my recommendation would be to install the mod only when you need it, and then remove it again after getting your mission done. 

Inspired by the Bigger Volcanoes mod, which was the only mod that came up in a search here when I was looking for a solution for yet-another-mission inside a volcano.

For game version Singularity 4.34
